rv.q: Much of our laughter comes from his ability to get theatergoers to transgress their own sensitivities with moments of intimate contact that almost always grow strangely sweet.
Garry—as enacted by Mr. Warren-Smith, whose double-barreled surname wouldn't suit the lowdown lunacy Garry gets up to—is a warmly ingratiating performer.
This beautiful tender city of humans needs someone as playfully joyful and talented as Damien Warren-Smith to suspend our vigilance and allow us to laugh at the glorious absurdity of everything.
This inimitable Australian comic is one of the funniest men on the planet and makes this hilarious and at times gross show a madcap and fast review of literature.

Happily, the delightfully zany “Garry Starr: Classic Penguins,” which has just arrived at Studio Seaview just weeks after delighting audiences at the Edinburgh Fringe, makes good on that concept to the nth degree.
Classic Penguins is some of the most original comedy on stage right now thanks to the trust Warren-Smith builds at each performance.
Garry Starr: Classic Penguins has a warm heart and a deep affection for the silliness of humanity.
I found a good deal to enjoy in the evening's inspired lunacy.

If you’re wincing or rolling your eyes, I did both, initially. But to Mr. Warren-Smith’s credit, he channels his inner clown with such breezy wit and benevolence that you may find “Garry Starr: Classic Penguins” charming in its unapologetic, ... Classic Penguins leans much too hard on immature provocation and not nearly enough on wit.
Far from a classic itself, Garry Starr may not be for everyone, but at just over an hour, you can’t quite write it off.
But if theater is about the power of the imagination, Garry Starr: Classic Penguins leaves nothing to the mind’s eye.
Garry Starr: Classic Penguins doesn't need me on its side to work—it just needs a room willing to go along for the ride, and it finds one.
Your enjoyment of Garry Starr will depend on your tolerance for its audacious mode of comedy as provocation.
The nudity eventually loses its shock value, and occasionally becomes incidental to the fun.

cn.t: Critics find this mostly-nude clown show outrageously silly and fearlessly uninhibited, with Warren-Smith's physical comedy and audience interaction earning laughs, though the crude humor and full-frontal approach isn't for everyone.
